- When sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment turns bearish (negative) mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward quickly; apply lagged correction, especially if sentiment shift is abrupt.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged bearish sentiment; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment remains negative for >5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply a 1–3% downward bias for days 1–7, then adjust based on sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen overconfidence in trending periods.
